interest: Japanese spying and propaganda in Hong Kong, 1936–39.
overview: Docket for 894.20246G (1936–39) on Japanese spying and propaganda in Hong Kong, including the Hong Kong News.

people.name: Kenkichi Fujiyama
people.role: Japanese national in Hong Kong arrested for photographing the harbour

people.name: John D. Hoover
people.role: U.S. Consular officer in Hong Kong

people.name: Addison E. Southard
people.role: U.S. Consul General in Hong Kong

subfiles.about: Reports on the arrest and investigation of Japanese national Kenkichi Fujiyama for photographing Hong Kong harbour.
subfiles.summary: Report on the arrest of Kenkichi Fujiyama for photographing Hong Kong harbour; no forbidden photos found.
subfiles.title: Despatch from Hoover on arrest of Kenkichi Fujiyama in Hong Kong

subfiles.about: Transmits newspaper clippings regarding criticism of the Hong Kong government for allowing a Japanese salvage company to work in a fortified area.
subfiles.summary: Southard forwards press criticism of letting a Japanese salvage firm work in a Hong Kong fortified area.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 137 from Southard on Japanese salvage operations in Hong Kong fortified area

subfiles.about: Reports on the publication of a new Japanese English-language propaganda newspaper in Hong Kong titled the Hong Kong News.
subfiles.summary: Southard reports the launch of the Japanese English-language Hong Kong News.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 493 from Southard on publication of the Hong Kong News

subfiles.about: Encloses a copy of an editorial from the Hong Kong Telegraph discussing the newly established Japanese propaganda organ, the Hong Kong News.
subfiles.summary: Southard sends a Hong Kong Telegraph editorial on the new Hong Kong News.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 494 from Southard enclosing Hong Kong Telegraph editorial on the Hong Kong News

subfiles.about: Furnishes intelligence and personal particulars regarding Japanese Secret Service agents Leonid Nicolaevitch Gutman and Leon Bielfeld.
subfiles.summary: British memo identifying Leonid Gutman and Leon Bielfeld as Japanese Secret Service agents.
subfiles.title: British Memorandum No. 167 on Japanese Secret Service agents Gutman and Bielfeld
